title: Max Value of Equation
summary: Given an array of points sorted by x-values and an integer k, find the maximum value of yi + yj + |xi - xj| for points (xi, yi) and (xj, yj) where |xi - xj| <= k and i < j.
statement: Given an array of points sorted by x-values and an integer k, find the maximum value of yi + yj + |xi - xj| for points (xi, yi) and (xj, yj) where |xi - xj| <= k and i < j. It is assured that at least one valid pair exists.
constraints: Points have strictly increasing x coordinates and at least one eligible pair.
Maximize yi+yj+|xi-xj| over i<j with xj-xi<=k.
hints: Maintain eligible prior yi-xi values in decreasing order.
Expire points farther than k before using the deque front, then insert the current transformed value monotonically.
The front is the maximum valid prior contribution for each j.
editorial: The front is the maximum valid prior contribution for each j.

tests.explanation: Only adjacent-distance-one pairs qualify; the first pair gives four.
The first two points give value three.
